# AutoAnts

> AutoAnts (the name is short for "automated assistants") is a Louisiana company founded and run by Lane Davis II. It builds websites,
> after-hours lead-intake systems, and AI-search visibility for Louisiana
> local businesses: trades, auto shops, salons, gyms and more. The first deliverable is always free: AutoAnts makes a
> company breakdown of a business from public information before any money changes hands.

## What AutoAnts does
- Three outcomes: get found (Google profile, listings, map work and AI answers), never miss a job (the automated assistants, the "Ants": missed-call text-back, web-form responder, scheduler, review ask, service-due and invoice reminders), and get the next job (social posts from the business's real jobs, permit-timed postcards, past-customer mailers and door hangers after each job)
- Starts with a free company breakdown: a 10-14 page look at the business made only from public information (Google and AI-answer visibility, reviews and listings next to nearby shops, what to fix first). Any video, preview site or sample postcard is shown inside the breakdown, not sold separately
- One ladder, four rungs, each including the one before (founding price for the
  first 3 shops on each rung, then the regular price; full list:
  https://autoants.com/prices/):
  1. Try one: one assistant live on the business's phone, $500 go-live, one
     time (then $750). The one assistant is missed-call text-back (the usual
     first one), the web-form responder, the scheduler, the review ask,
     service-due reminders or invoice reminders. Live within 7 days of "go",
     or the $500 back. Texts run on the business's own Twilio account
  2. Office Manager: $750 setup + $500/month, then $1,500 setup + $750/month.
     Missed-call text-back, web-form responder, scheduler with quote
     follow-up, review ask, service-due reminders (pre-season tune-ups for
     HVAC), invoice reminders, call tracking matched to jobs, a light social
     version, and email cleanup in the setup
  3. Growth: $1,000 setup + $1,500/month, then $1,750/month. Everything in
     Office Manager plus Google profile, listings and map work; 2 new
     service-and-town or AI-answer pages a month and a monthly check of what
     AI answers say; website hosting and upkeep (a site rebuild of up to 5
     pages in setup when the site is costing calls; a preview site goes live
     on the business's own domain here); social posts from real jobs twice a
     month, including weather-alert campaigns; review replies drafted weekly;
     the citywide permit-timed postcard for the trade (cards $1.30 each). A
     30-minute call monthly; next-business-day response
  4. Pro: $1,500 setup + $2,500/month, then $3,000/month. Everything in Growth
     plus weekly social posts with animated Shorts, 4 new pages a month, a
     past-customer anniversary mailer, door hangers around each finished job,
     the "next available" booking box on the phone homepage, and a responder
     for Facebook/Instagram inquiries. A 30-minute call every two weeks;
     same-business-day response
- Same on every rung: the business owns every account, page, listing and
  list; no result promises. Office Manager, Growth and Pro have a 90-day
  minimum, then run month to month, cancel by email
- Scoped once a business is on Growth: the receptionist (an AI that answers
  when nobody can and always says it is an AI; minutes written into the
  agreement) and anything else not listed above
- Operations Math by autoants: the one separate line, for big shops (routes,
  schedules, cutting, loads). A $1,500 30-day pilot, credited to month one,
  then priced by size
- The assessment: $500 flat. A recorded 45-minute interview, then a bound,
  printed report on what to fix first and what each fix is worth in the
  owner's own numbers. Credited toward setup if they continue within 30 days.
  Founding price; $1,000 after two reference clients

## The assistants ("Ants", one job each; the owner approves what goes to customers)
- Text-Back Ant: texts back a missed call within seconds
- Responder Ant: answers a new web or social lead within seconds
- Scheduler Ant: turns quote requests into estimates and booked appointments
- Reviewer Ant: asks every customer for a review, the same way every time
- Receptionist Ant: answers calls the owner can't pick up, says it's an AI,
  texts the details to the owner
- Scout Ant: local listings and AI-search visibility
- Reminder Ant: reaches past customers who agreed to hear from the business
- Promoter Ant: short job videos and local ads

## How it works
1. AutoAnts makes a free company breakdown of the business from public
   information
2. If the owner wants to try one piece: $500 one time puts one assistant live
   on their phone, within 7 days of the go-ahead or the $500 back (the only
   promise AutoAnts makes)
3. Bigger needs move up the ladder: Office Manager, Growth, Pro. No contract to
   start; monthly rungs have a 90-day minimum, then month to month

## Who it's for
- Home services and trades (tree, HVAC, roofing, plumbing, landscaping): the core focus
- Also offered to auto shops, salons and nail spas, gyms and studios, pet businesses, restaurants and event businesses, and professional services (accountants, insurance, real estate, tutors)
- Dental and medical offices: not yet; patient information needs a HIPAA program first
- Details: https://autoants.com/who-we-help.html

## Why customers choose it
- Owner-run: owners deal with Lane directly, not a call center; the
  business is built on doing only what it would put its name on
- The free-first model: a free company breakdown before paying anything
- Flat, quoted-up-front pricing on one published ladder
- Legitimate-only optimization policy: no paid link placements, no seeded
  or undisclosed mentions, no astroturfing — the fixes are real signals
  (complete profiles, real reviews, consistent listings, structured data)

## Findings from New Orleans public records
- Permits Pulled: a free monthly report for New Orleans trades owners on what
  public records say about where the work is (counts only)
- Findings: re-roof permits peak in April (about 49% above an average month); HVAC permits peak in April-May and October, not summer; standby generator permits ran 8 times higher in 2022 after Hurricane Ida (714 vs about 86 a year in 2016-2019). Source: data.nola.gov 72f9-bi28, pulled 2026-10-08

## Contact
- Contact: the form at https://autoants.com/#contact
- Service area: Louisiana — Greater New Orleans, Baton Rouge, and the
  Northshore first
